root_cause: The docs example docs_src/metadata/tutorial001_1_py39.py sets license_info={"name": "Apache 2.0", "identifier": "MIT"}. That SPDX identifier does not match the license name.
best_solution: Grep the repo for '"identifier": "MIT"'. It appears once, in the license_info dict of docs_src/metadata/tutorial001_1_py39.py. Change it to '"identifier": "Apache-2.0"'. Leave the name "Apache 2.0" as it is. The statement gives the exact replacement string, so this one-line change is the whole fix. The example's OpenAPI output ends up in the tutorial test's expected schema, so the value has to match exactly.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_tutorial/test_metadata/test_tutorial001_1.py::test_openapi_schema now expects the /openapi.json info.license to be exactly {"name": "Apache 2.0", "identifier": "Apache-2.0"}. The name must stay unchanged, and the SPDX string must be exactly 'Apache-2.0' (hyphen, no space).
locating_signals: The statement does not name the file. It gives the wrong value (`MIT`), the right value (`Apache-2.0`) and the context ('license identifier in documentation'). Grepping for the literal 'identifier' with 'MIT' in docs_src/ finds the only hit. The file name metadata/tutorial001_1 matches the test path.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8) passed in the Kaggle env. Each produced the same one-line patch as the gold (391 chars). Pod runs took 36-38 s and 10-14 calls.
generalizable_lesson: If a statement names the wrong literal and the right one, grep the repo for the wrong literal and make only that replacement. Don't also 'fix' nearby fields (here the license name). Docs example files (docs_src/, examples/) are often run by tests that compare the output exactly, so treat them as code: keep the exact string, including case and hyphens.
acceptable_alternatives: Only the exact string 'Apache-2.0' in that one file passes. Changing the name field too, or using a variant such as 'Apache 2.0' or 'apache-2.0' for the identifier, would fail the exact schema comparison.
